ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with a distinct cream-colored glandular fold along its flanks. It features a pointed snout and granular skin texture. It belongs to the family Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes glandulosus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, prominent glandular fold extending from behind the eye to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes glandulosus* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Southern Bubble-nest Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of the Western Ghats' rainforest canopy.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes glandulosus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It lays small clutches of eggs in vegetation during the monsoon (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes glandulosus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Southern Bubble-nest Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps or "tinks" while perched on low vegetation in humid evergreen forests.
